samples.name: quarter-turn
samples.derivation: Local x axis becomes world +y and local y becomes world -x; the 100x60 rect covers x [50,110), y [70,170), area 100*60 = 6000, center maps to (80,120).

1.derivation: world area = local area * |scaleX * scaleY| * scale^2; centroid = mapped local center

2.derivation: world area = local area * |scaleX * scaleY| * scale^2; centroid = mapped local center

samples.name: nonuniform-scale
samples.derivation: 40x20 local rect scaled by (3, 0.5) becomes 120x10 at (30,50); area 1200.

1.derivation: world area = local area * |scaleX * scaleY| * scale^2; centroid = mapped local center

2.derivation: world area = local area * |scaleX * scaleY| * scale^2; centroid = mapped local center

samples.name: nonuniform-rotation
samples.derivation: Scale first: 40x20 -> 80x60, rotate 90 degrees -> 60x80, translate to (140,40); area 40*20*2*3 = 4800, bbox [140,40,200,120].

1.derivation: world area = local area * |scaleX * scaleY| * scale^2; centroid = mapped local center

2.derivation: world area = local area * |scaleX * scaleY| * scale^2; centroid = mapped local center

samples.name: combined-clip-rotation-scale
samples.derivation: The group matrix (scale 1.5/0.75, rotate 25, translate 80/50) carries a 120x100 local clip; determinant 1.5*0.75 = 1.125 gives world area 13500. The 400x300 child overshoots every side, so coverage is the clip area and the centroid is the mapped clip center (80,60); scale 2 multiplies coverage by four.

1.derivation: clip local area * |group scaleX * scaleY| * scale^2; centroid = mapped clip center; child is oversized

2.derivation: clip local area * |group scaleX * scaleY| * scale^2; centroid = mapped clip center; child is oversized

samples.name: nested-clips
samples.derivation: Both clips must contain the mapped pixel center: the intersection is 50x25 at world (120,70), center (145,82.5), area 1250.

1.derivation: outer clip world x [120,200) y [70,140); inner translation moves its clip to x [110,170) y [65,95); intersection x [120,170) y [70,95) = 50x25 = 1250; child 400x400 exceeds both

2.derivation: outer clip world x [120,200) y [70,140); inner translation moves its clip to x [110,170) y [65,95); intersection x [120,170) y [70,95) = 50x25 = 1250; child 400x400 exceeds both

samples.name: layer-order
samples.derivation: Later layers paint over earlier ones: 3600 blue pixels and 6400 red pixels at scale 1, each count multiplied by four at scale 2.

1.derivation: red x [10,110) y [10,110) and blue x [50,110) y [50,110) overlap in 60x60; blue is later and opaque so it owns the overlap: 3600 blue, 10000-3600 = 6400 red

2.derivation: red x [10,110) y [10,110) and blue x [50,110) y [50,110) overlap in 60x60; blue is later and opaque so it owns the overlap: 3600 blue, 10000-3600 = 6400 red

samples.name: edge-on-pixel-center
samples.derivation: Left edge at x=10.5 and top at y=20.5 coincide with pixel centers 10 and 20; half-open bounds put those columns inside, giving exactly 100x60 = 6000 pixels.

1.derivation: world area = local area * |scaleX * scaleY| * scale^2; centroid = mapped local center

2.derivation: world area = local area * |scaleX * scaleY| * scale^2; centroid = mapped local center

samples.name: edge-on-pixel-center-full-turn
samples.derivation: A 360 degree turn is the identity, so the same 6000-pixel edge must remain; a residual sin(2*pi) = -2.4e-16 would move the left edge and delete a pixel column.

1.derivation: world area = local area * |scaleX * scaleY| * scale^2; centroid = mapped local center

2.derivation: world area = local area * |scaleX * scaleY| * scale^2; centroid = mapped local center

samples.name: ellipse
samples.derivation: Unit-circle test in local space: coverage must match the analytic ellipse area within one percent.

1.derivation: semi-axes 60 and 40 -> area pi*60*40 = 7539.8; sampled pixel centers deviate only along the boundary

2.derivation: semi-axes 60 and 40 -> area pi*60*40 = 7539.8; sampled pixel centers deviate only along the boundary

samples.name: polygon
samples.derivation: Even-odd fill of the triangle must cover its analytic area within one percent.
